items.description: `_RELEASE_KEYS` gains `reconciler`, `deployed`, `autoSync`, `repo`, `targetRevision`: a release.yaml carrying all five passes the allowlist check, while any other key still fails loud with a non-zero exit.
`discover_releases` skips non-`jenkins` reconcilers by direct file read — no `deploy config` subprocess per release and no chart-existence trip.
Helm-bearing verbs (`deploy`, `template`, `stop`, `uninstall`) refuse `argo-cd` releases with a clear message and a non-zero exit.
The state-mutating Terraform verbs `apply`, `destroy` and `import` refuse an `argo-cd` release too, so nothing writes against the old, emptied HelmCharts Terraform state key (D32).

The genuinely read-only inspection verbs — `plan`, `output`, `config`, `wait` — stay usable against a migrated release; being able to look at one is worth keeping. `config` in particular never refuses, since `gen_architecture` calls it for every prd stage and does not catch a non-zero exit.

`reconciler:` defaults to `jenkins` when absent: both a missing key and a missing release.yaml resolve and enumerate as Jenkins-owned, and every release that exists today behaves exactly as it does now.
`chart: null` keeps HelmCharts release resolution working once `charts/<app>/` is deleted, using the existing infra-only value and no new mechanism.

A registered `reconciler: argo-cd` entry does not break `gen-architecture`, whatever shape the entry takes — `chart:` omitted, `chart: null`, or an `upstream: {repo, chart, version}` block: the run completes and the migrated app drops out of the model, rather than failing `Jenkinsfile.architecture` and losing the whole artifact. Silent non-coverage is the accepted outcome; a failure is not.
A registered `reconciler: argo-cd` entry does not break `audit-prd-orphans` or `recommend-resources` — each still runs to completion over `configs/prd/`.
The Jenkins deploy pipeline's release list and `collect-versions` survive a registered entry: both produce their output without a traceback, and the migrated release simply gets no deploy stage.

items.area: Ruling — how this slice is proven
items.description: `kc project test`, run from the HelmCharts repo root, runs the new unit tests and is green; the repo carries a `.kubecoder/project.yaml` declaring the curated entry points and **no** `.kubecoder/config.yaml`.

items.area: Ruling — how this slice is proven
items.description: pytest arrives as a Poetry dependency group in HelmCharts' own pyproject.toml and the container needs nothing new: a `poetry install --only main` — what the iac image and CI use — installs no test dependency, and the Jenkinsfile is unchanged.

A release whose `chart:` overrides the config-directory name resolves through the local-chart path instead of falling through to the upstream-repo path and raising; the fix is provably inert for every current release, none of which sets a top-level `chart:`.

items.area: Ruling — how this slice is proven
items.description: The suite is hermetic: `kc project test` is green with no cluster, no network and no `helm`/`kubectl`/`terraform` subprocess, and leaves the repo's real `configs/` tree unmodified.

`refresh-secrets` refuses an `argo-cd` release: it is not an inspection verb — it annotates the namespace's ExternalSecrets and then rolls their consumers, which in a migrated namespace are Argo-owned pod templates.

`_UPSTREAM_KEYS` is not widened and every `jenkins`-owned release keeps every check exactly as strict as today — the chart-existence check and the `upstream:` block's exactly-{repo_name, repo_url, chart} check both still fire for them; only an entry that names a non-`jenkins` reconciler is exempt.
